findings.message:
Task acceptance not fulfilled: the review found that the candidate does not satisfy source issue #83. Change the candidate so it satisfies everything the issue requires; the reviewer's acceptance evidence:
- Implemented: enrollment, account-create and challenge buckets are applied before password hashing and before challenge/account writes in /api/auth/password/register, /api/auth/register/start, /api/auth/register/finish and /api/auth/login/start.
- Missing: /api/auth/password/continue (src/passport.ts:759-802) still hashes an unauthenticated supplied password and calls createUserWithPassword for unknown emails without any bucket, so the reported CPU and account-spam path remains.
- Missing: expired challenge cleanup is unreachable because list and atomic check both filter expired keys, so challenge rows accumulate in D1; no cleanup job exists in kv-service.
- Missing: no test files changed for password-registration CPU budgets, challenge issuance or distributed attempts, and the password semaphore is isolate-local rather than global.

[P1] Password continue path bypasses new enrollment limits

The new `allowEnrollment`/`allowAccountCreation` guards are only applied in `handlePasswordRegister`; the sibling unauthenticated `POST /api/auth/password/continue` path (lines 759-802) still calls `hashPassword` and `createUserWithPassword` for any unknown email without consulting a bucket. An attacker can bypass all of the new registration limits and keep burning 600k-iteration PBKDF2 while creating unlimited accounts.

src/passport.ts:689-691

[P1] Expired challenge cleanup never deletes records

`activeChallengeCount` intends to delete expired challenge records, but every `AuthStore.list` implementation filters expired entries before yielding (the D1 query has `expires_at > now`, and `MemoryStore` skips expired rows), so `isExpired(entry.value.expiresAt)` is never true. Even if an expired entry were yielded, `atomic().check(entry)` fails for an expired key because the KV service check also excludes expired rows. Expired challenge rows are therefore never removed and authoritative D1 state keeps growing.

src/auth_store.ts:945-953

[P2] One source can exhaust the global enrollment bucket

`allowEnrollment` checks a global 10/hour bucket before the 10/hour source and 3/hour identity buckets, so ten requests from one source (even all for the same email, since identity is checked last) consume the entire global budget. After that every password registration and passkey registration start returns 429 for up to an hour, including signed-in users adding a passkey; remove the global bucket or size and order it so one source cannot lock out all enrollment.

src/passport.ts:155-162

[P2] Active-challenge cap can lock out all WebAuthn starts

`MAX_ACTIVE_CHALLENGES` is 256 while `/login/start` permits 100 challenge issuances per minute and a challenge lives for 5 minutes, so allowed issuance over one TTL is about 500. A distributed client staying inside the issued limits can keep the shared bucket full; `saveChallenge` then returns null and every login/registration start gets 429, locking out all users including administrators.

src/auth_store.ts:941-944

[P2] Password work limiter is isolate-local, not global

The semaphore is module-scoped, so each Worker isolate gets its own two slots; in the Worker runtime each hash is dispatched to a fresh Durable Object (`getByName(crypto.randomUUID())` in `src/worker.ts`), so concurrent PBKDF2 work is not bounded globally as the task requires. Enforce the limit in a shared component such as the hasher Durable Object or a single named object.

src/password.ts:9-14

summary: The patch adds useful guards but does not close the unauthenticated password account-creation path, never actually deletes expired challenges, and introduces globally exhaustible enrollment/challenge caps; required regressions are absent.
